title: State and checkpointing
summary: Whether the work in progress is saved to a hidden git ref before a gated command or a plan step, who takes the checkpoint, and how many are kept.

questions.prompt: Who takes a checkpoint before a gated command?

options.label: The pre-tool hook, with an instruction where no hook runs
options.tradeoff: Automatic on every host with a working pre-tool hook, at the cost of one working-tree snapshot per gated command; other hosts rely on the agent following the instruction.

options.label: Instruction only
options.tradeoff: Nothing runs by itself; depends on the agent taking the checkpoint.

options.label: Before a gated command
options.tradeoff: Rare moments where rollback matters (force-push, hard reset, rm -rf, publishing); costs one snapshot each.

options.label: Before a plan step starts
options.tradeoff: Every step can be rolled back to its start; one more snapshot per step.

options.label: The 10 newest
options.tradeoff: Bounded size, nothing to clean up; an older checkpoint is gone after 10 newer ones.

options.label: All of them
options.tradeoff: Nothing is lost, but refs and the objects they keep alive accumulate.

decisions.title: Work is checkpointed before a gated action
decisions.body:
## Decision

The pre-tool hook saves the working tree to a hidden git ref before a gated command (triggers: {{answer.triggers}}; keep: {{answer.retention}}), and the agent does it where no hook runs (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A hard reset or a recursive delete cannot be undone from the host (decision 0097); a checkpoint costs a few kilobytes.

guardrails.title: A gated action is preceded by a checkpoint

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given work in progress must be recoverable after an irreversible command (0097), a checkpoint must exist before the command runs, since the host cannot undo what a shell command did.

enforcement.check: The pre-tool hook takes a checkpoint before a gated command
Where no hook runs, run `go-getter checkpoint create --label <what>` before a gated command

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Before a gated command, or a plan step when the project checkpoints those, a checkpoint of the working tree exists: the pre-tool hook takes it, or you run `go-getter checkpoint create --label <what>` where no hook runs. Restore with `go-getter checkpoint restore` (see the procedure).

procedures.title: Restore work from a checkpoint
procedures.body:
## Procedure

1. `go-getter checkpoint list`: newest first, with the label and ref.
2. `go-getter checkpoint restore <label>` shows what would change (M modified, D deleted, A created since) and changes nothing.
3. If the list is right, add `--yes`: it puts back the M and D files in the working tree only. Files created since stay; remove them yourself if unwanted.
4. A host's own rewind or restore command may undo editor changes, but not what a shell command did: use the checkpoint for that.

decisions.title: Checkpointing is advisory
decisions.body:
## Decision

Agents are told to take a checkpoint before a gated command; nothing takes one automatically (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted the risk for less machinery (decision 0097).

guardrails.title: Agents checkpoint before a gated action

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the project chose no mechanical checkpoint, the rule rests on the agent following it.

enforcement.check: Run `go-getter checkpoint create --label <what>` before a gated command

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Before a gated command, run `go-getter checkpoint create --label <what>`. Advisory (tier 1): nothing takes it for you. Restore with `go-getter checkpoint restore`.

decisions.title: A checkpoint is taken before a gated command
decisions.body:
## Decision

The pre-tool hook takes a checkpoint before any command in the gated catalog (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Force-pushes, hard resets and recursive deletes cannot be undone from the host, and a checkpoint costs a few kilobytes (decision 0097).

decisions.title: A checkpoint is taken before a plan step starts
decisions.body:
## Decision

`go-getter plan start` takes a checkpoint before it marks a step in progress (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Every step can then be rolled back to its start, for one more snapshot per step (decision 0097).

decisions.title: The 10 newest checkpoints are kept
decisions.body:
## Decision

Checkpoints beyond the 10 newest are pruned when a new one is taken (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Size stays bounded with nothing to clean up by hand (decision 0097).

decisions.title: Every checkpoint is kept
decisions.body:
## Decision

Checkpoints are never pruned automatically (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); `go-getter checkpoint prune` removes them by hand.

## Why

Nothing is lost, at the price of refs and the objects they keep alive accumulating (decision 0097).
